channel.title: Colorado Public Radio - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Colorado Public Radio (cpr.org)

item.title: More ‘No Kings’ protests planned for March 28 as outrage spreads over Minneapolis deaths
item.description: The October “No Kings” rally in Colorado drew thousands of protesters across the state, from Grand Junction to the Eastern Plains, but there are no immediate local plans for the day in March.

item.title: State trooper injured in car crash trying to stop wrong-way driver on I-25
item.description: The officer was taken to the hospital with serious but non-life-threatening injuries.

item.title: Crisosto Apache named Colorado’s newest poet laureate
item.description: Apache is the first indigenous poet to hold the position.

item.title: As the Trump administration targets NCAR, scientists rally to defend the ‘mothership’ of atmospheric research
item.description: A letter published by the National Science Foundation asks for ideas to dismantle the research hub. Scientists are responding en masse.

item.title: Federal judge blocks a Trump administration order that threatened SNAP in Colorado
item.description: The administration would have required Colorado to interview more than 100,000 households in its SNAP program within 30 days.

item.title: Colorado lawmakers face angry crowds over ICE actions, Gaza
item.description: In recent days, Sen. Michael Bennet and Rep. Diana DeGette have been heckled at public appearances. Other lawmakers are worried they’re next.

item.title: Former Colorado state senator convicted of felonies for fabricating letters amid ethics investigation
item.description: Sonya Jaquez Lewis, a Boulder County Democrat, was convicted by a Denver jury of attempting to influence a public servant and forgery.

item.title: Cherry Creek schools superintendent resigns following ‘toxic culture’ investigation
item.description: The superintendent's wife is the chief human resource officer, which employs say created a conflict of interest.

item.title: Problem-solving students take on the shortage of teachers of color in Colorado
item.description: Northglenn High schoolers present evidence and data on how teacher diversity is a benefit to their education.

item.title: Congress is headed toward another partial government shutdown
item.description: Colorado’s Senators want Homeland Security funding pulled from a minibus government funding bill after federal immigration agents shot a Minneapolis man this past weekend.
